statusText: Tail falls to 17%. Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The 13:30Z U.S. cash open, which the prior hour flagged as the window's main conditional risk, produced no downside continuation. Cash NDX trades 31,097.54, -0.20%, at its 31,102.79 session high after opening near 30,918.77, and NQ Dec26 has recovered to 31,257.00, narrowing the loss to -0.46% from -0.78% at the session low. VIX has decayed to 15.40, close to its 15.31 session low and well below the 16.02 high. The long end eased to 10Y 5.29% and 30Y 5.65%. Stress stays elevated at 63% because WTI is +4.1% at $91.90 and Brent +4.3% at $104.51 on record Hormuz tanker attacks, but that oil impulse now conflicts with easing yields and a decaying VIX rather than aligning with them.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON with Tail at 17%, inside the 0-19% low band and well below the 25% blocking threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 17:00Z-19:00Z, spanning the 30-year bond auction and the Fed Musalem speech, where conditional Tail ridges to 21% and maps to WATCH. No slot in the 24-hour window reaches the blocking threshold. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 absorbs the U.S. cash open without downside continuation as VIX decays to session lows, pulling Tail into the low band while a 4% oil shock keeps Stress elevated
body: The 14:00Z first full cash hour resolved the conditional risk the prior assessment had flagged. The 13:30Z open did not extend the Globex decline: cash NDX opened lower, printed 30,918.77, then rallied to 31,097.54, -62.54 or -0.20% against a 31,160.08 prior close, and is trading at its 31,102.79 session high as of 14:26Z. NQ Dec26 is 31,257.00, -145.25 or -0.46% against a 31,402.25 prior close, corroborated independently at 31,238.75 with -0.52% and the same reference close. The 31,119.75 session low printed in the 11:00Z hour has now stood for roughly three and a half hours, and the day's loss has narrowed in five steps from -0.78% through -0.70%, -0.59% and -0.52% to -0.46%. VIX is 15.40, +2.12% against a 15.08 prior close, sitting near the 15.31 session low after peaking at 16.02. This is the observed negation of the pathological no-retracement path Tail measures: retracements are occurring, the opening auction did not continue, and implied volatility is decaying. Tail therefore falls from 21% to 17%, into the low band. Stress remains elevated at 63%. WTI is $91.90, +4.10%, and Brent $104.51, +4.30%, after Kpler data showed 10 tankers struck in the Strait of Hormuz between September 28 and October 4, a record weekly count against a previous high of six, with only seven transits on Tuesday, the fewest since July 23. A Gulf Coast tropical storm has also shut in production. Treasury yields are 2Y 4.81%, 10Y 5.29% and 30Y 5.65%, near multidecade highs but with the long end slightly lower on the day. That is the key cross-asset read: the oil impulse is not confirmed by yields or by VIX, so it raises the difficulty of the environment rather than establishing a one-way path. Initial jobless claims printed 197K against a 200K consensus, a fourth straight week near 57-year lows, while continuing claims rose to 1.716 million. Remaining scheduled catalysts today are the 17:00Z 30-year bond auction and the 17:40Z Fed Musalem speech, the basis for the narrow 17:00Z-19:00Z danger window where conditional Tail ridges to 21%.

lookbackSummary: The 24 hours to 13:00Z contain two complete risk cycles. Tail opened the window at 23% during Wednesday's U.S. afternoon, decayed steadily to a 10% trough by 03:00Z as the overnight session mean-reverted, then rebuilt from 06:00Z as the Hormuz oil shock and the long-end yield move reasserted themselves. It reached 23% at 11:00Z when a multi-hour base gave way and NQ printed its 31,119.75 session low, held 22% at 12:00Z, then eased to 21% at 13:00Z as the low survived its first two hours. Stress climbed almost monotonically across the window, from 47% overnight to a 66% peak at 12:00Z, reflecting an environment that grew harder even while the price path stayed recoverable. Confidence held in a tight 86-89% band throughout, and no hour of the window was unavailable.
outlookSummary: Conditional Tail stays inside the low band for 22 of the 24 slots and never approaches the 25% blocking threshold. It holds at 17-18% through the remainder of the U.S. cash session, ridges to a 21% window peak in the 17:00Z hour that contains the 30-year bond auction and the Fed Musalem speech, eases to 20% during auction digestion at 18:00Z, then decays through the cash close to a 12% trough across the 00:00Z-03:00Z Asian hours. The narrow 17:00Z-19:00Z danger window covers only the two WATCH slots. From 04:00Z the path climbs gradually to 19% by Friday 13:00Z as European and U.S. participation returns and the window closes immediately before the 14:00Z Michigan preliminary release, whose inflation-expectations components carry extra weight given the oil impulse. Confidence decays from 89% to 75% across the window as the forecast moves from observed structure to assumption.
